top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: The day is dominated by the Middle East: tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran held mass funeral processions for Ayatollah Khamenei, while Trump warned of a deal or the US 'finishing the job.' NATO's summit pushed arms deals and Ukraine's air-defence needs after deadly Russian strikes near Kyiv. Markets wobbled as South Korea's KOSPI plunged about 8%.

stories.headline: Tankers struck in Strait of Hormuz as Iran mourns Khamenei
stories.summary: At least one oil tanker was hit by an 'unknown projectile' in the Strait of Hormuz region, a maritime agency said, as huge crowds in Iran held funeral processions for Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Tehran says there will be no talks unless President Trump halts his threats; Trump said there would either be a deal with Iran or the US would 'finish the job.'

stories.headline: NATO summit spotlights arms deals and a push to keep Trump on side
stories.summary: At the NATO summit, allies showcased new defence purchases — including Swedish Saab early-warning aircraft over a US rival and a strategic A400M airlift fleet — as members pushed to win over President Trump on burden-sharing. Alliance chief Mark Rutte said talks would also cover tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Russian strikes kill 24 near Kyiv; Zelensky to press NATO for air defences
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed 24 people in the Kyiv region on the eve of the NATO summit, and President Zelensky is pressing allies for more air-defence systems, the BBC reported. Separately, Kyiv says its forces struck eight Russian 'shadow fleet' tankers — a claim not independently verified.

stories.headline: Explosions injure 18 in Damascus during Macron's visit
stories.summary: Explosions struck near a hotel housing French President Emmanuel Macron during a visit to Syria's capital, injuring 18 people, the BBC reported. The blasts came as Macron met Syria's new authorities; French officials said he was unharmed.

stories.headline: South Korea's KOSPI plunges about 8%, triggering circuit breakers
stories.summary: South Korea's KOSPI tumbled about 8%, triggering trading circuit breakers for the sixth time this year amid a sharp sell-off in AI-related stocks, CNA reported.

stories.headline: French court shortens Le Pen's ban, opening door to a presidential run
stories.summary: A French appeals court shortened Marine Le Pen's ban from public office but ordered her to wear an electronic ankle tag, a ruling that could clear the way for a presidential bid, The Straits Times reported.

stories.headline: China storm death toll rises to 15 as Typhoon Maysak floods the south
stories.summary: The death toll from storms in China rose to 15 with hundreds injured, as Typhoon Maysak triggered catastrophic flooding and put the city of Nanning on top alert, CNA reported.

stories.headline: More than 1,000 arrested in global human-trafficking crackdown
stories.summary: More than 1,000 people were arrested in a coordinated international operation against human-trafficking networks, the BBC reported.

stories.headline: China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, sources say
stories.summary: Chinese AI firm DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip, sources told CNA, a move that could reduce reliance on foreign semiconductors amid US export curbs.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Parliament was all about transport: proposed jail and lower alcohol limits for dangerous and drink-driving, a new offence for holding your phone at the wheel, S$800m for transport research, and help for cabbies and private-hire drivers facing the driverless-vehicle shift. NEA flagged a fast-growing dengue cluster in Yio Chu Kang. Expect thundery showers today. In lighter news, Jackie Chan charmed a local school.

stories.headline: Tougher penalties for dangerous driving, lower drink-driving limits proposed
stories.summary: The Government proposed harsher penalties for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt, lower blood-alcohol limits, and jail for first-time drink-driving offenders, under changes tabled in Parliament.

stories.headline: Holding a phone while driving set to become an offence
stories.summary: Under proposed changes to road traffic law, drivers caught merely holding a mobile phone while driving could face fines of up to S$1,000 and up to six months' jail, CNA and The Straits Times reported.

stories.headline: Taxi, private-hire drivers to get support amid driverless-vehicle shift
stories.summary: Taxi and private-hire drivers will get career-conversion programmes and up to S$1,600 in training incentives to take up new roles as Singapore expands autonomous vehicles, CNA reported.

stories.headline: Singapore to invest S$800 million in transport research over five years
stories.summary: Singapore will invest S$800 million in transport research and innovation over the next five years under RIE2030, as Parliament backed a long-term transport strategy, CNA and The Straits Times reported.

stories.headline: NEA flags fast-growing dengue cluster in Yio Chu Kang
stories.summary: The National Environment Agency reported a fast-growing dengue cluster in the Yio Chu Kang/Lentor area with 135 cases so far, urging residents to remove stagnant water and take precautions.

stories.headline: 17 arrested, over S$720,000 seized in islandwide gambling bust
stories.summary: Police arrested 17 people and seized more than S$720,000 in an islandwide operation against illegal gambling, The Straits Times reported.

stories.headline: Jackie Chan visits Singapore school and breaks into song
stories.summary: Actor Jackie Chan visited Pei Chun Public School, telling pupils 'without dreams, you'll never succeed' and breaking into song before he left, Mothership reported.

stories.headline: Boon Lay woman fights upstairs noise with a screaming rubber chicken
stories.summary: A 62-year-old Boon Lay resident losing sleep over noise from the unit above has hit back with a screaming rubber chicken and banging pots, in a neighbourly dispute that has drawn attention online, Mothership reported.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Russia–Ukraine is the most active theatre: Russian strikes killed 24 in the Kyiv region ahead of the NATO summit, where Zelensky is pressing for air defences, while Kyiv claims strikes on Russian 'shadow-fleet' tankers. In the Middle East, a fragile US–Iran truce holds as Iran mourns Khamenei and tankers are hit in the Strait of Hormuz; in Gaza, Israeli strikes continue, Hamas says it will dissolve its governing body, and Israel–Lebanon talks are set for Rome.

theatres.name: Russia–Ukraine
theatres.status: Heavy Russian strikes on Kyiv; Ukraine claims hits on Russia's 'shadow fleet' as Zelensky lobbies NATO for air defence

timeline.event: Russian strikes kill 24 people in the Kyiv region on the eve of the NATO summit.
Analysis of intercept data suggests Ukraine is increasingly struggling to shoot down Russian ballistic missiles.
Zelensky to press the NATO summit for more air-defence systems after intense Russian strikes.
Ukraine says its forces struck eight Russian 'shadow fleet' tankers (Kyiv claim, not independently verified).

theatres.name: US–Iran / Strait of Hormuz
theatres.status: Fragile truce holds; Iran mourns Khamenei; tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz

timeline.event: Trump says there will either be a deal with Iran or the US will 'finish the job.'
An oil tanker is hit by an 'unknown projectile' in the Strait of Hormuz region, a maritime agency says.
Huge crowds in Iran hold funeral processions for Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei; Tehran says no talks unless Trump halts threats.

theatres.name: Israel–Gaza / Lebanon
theatres.status: Sporadic strikes continue; Hamas says it will dissolve its Gaza governing body; Israel–Lebanon talks set for Rome

timeline.event: Hamas announces the dissolution of its Gaza governing body.
Israel and Lebanon agree to hold talks in Rome in mid-July.
Israeli strikes kill two people in Gaza, medics say.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: WHO says the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is still expanding — 1,481 confirmed cases and 454 deaths as of early July, a fatality rate near 31%, with over 100 health workers infected and one imported case in France. The Andes hantavirus cluster from the MV Hondius cruise holds at 13 cases and 3 deaths, human-to-human spread confirmed aboard but off-ship risk low. WHO has also flagged a Nipah case in Kerala.

outbreaks.name: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) — DR Congo & Uganda
outbreaks.status: Still in expansion phase (WHO, 3 Jul); crude CFR ~31%
outbreaks.scope_note: Confirmed cases only: DRC 1,460 cases / 452 deaths (as of 1 Jul, CFR 30.9%), Uganda 20 / 2, plus one imported case in France linked to DRC. 102 health workers infected. Source: WHO DON612.

outbreaks.name: Andes hantavirus — MV Hondius cruise
outbreaks.status: Human-to-human spread confirmed aboard ship; off-ship risk low
outbreaks.scope_note: 12 confirmed + 1 probable case, all M/V Hondius travellers; 3 deaths (ages 69, 70, 79); CFR 23%. Contacts traced across 33 countries/territories. Source: WHO DON611.

stories.headline: WHO says DR Congo Ebola outbreak still in 'expansion phase'
stories.summary: WHO said the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo remains in an expansion phase, with confirmed cases and deaths rising rapidly; the latest WHO figures put the outbreak at 1,481 confirmed cases and 454 deaths across DRC, Uganda and one imported case in France.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Vulnerabilities lead this cycle. A max-severity Adobe ColdFusion flaw (CVE-2026-48282, CVSS 10) is being exploited within hours of disclosure; a critical Gitea Docker flaw (CVE-2026-20896) is being probed in the wild; BeyondTrust patched critical auth-bypass bugs in its remote-access tools; and a China-aligned group is exploiting Roundcube webmail at universities. Also notable: a 16-year-old 'Januscape' Linux KVM VM-escape flaw, a hidden backdoor in Tenda routers, and Iran-linked hackers deploying a new 'Cavern' C2 against Israeli targets.

stories.headline: Critical Gitea Docker flaw being probed in the wild
stories.summary: Threat actors are attempting to exploit CVE-2026-20896 (CVSS 9.8), a critical flaw in Gitea Docker images, roughly 13 days after disclosure, Sysdig said via The Hacker News. Administrators running affected Gitea container images should patch.

stories.headline: China-aligned hackers exploit Roundcube webmail at universities
stories.summary: A suspected China-aligned cluster is exploiting Roundcube webmail flaws — including CVE-2024-42009 (CVSS 9.3) — at physics and engineering departments of US and Canadian universities, The Hacker News reported. Organisations running Roundcube should ensure they are patched.

stories.headline: BeyondTrust patches critical auth-bypass flaws in remote-access tools
stories.summary: BeyondTrust released fixes for two critical flaws in Remote Support (RS) and Privileged Remote Access (PRA). The headline bug, CVE-2026-40138 (CVSS 9.2), is an authentication weakness that could let unauthenticated attackers take control of affected appliances; about 2,000 instances remain exposed online, though no exploitation is yet reported. Two high-severity issues were also patched.

stories.headline: 16-year-old 'Januscape' Linux KVM flaw lets guest VMs escape to host
stories.summary: A use-after-free bug in Linux's KVM hypervisor, dubbed 'Januscape' (CVE-2026-53359), can be triggered from a guest VM to corrupt host-kernel state and escape to the host on Intel and AMD x86 systems, The Hacker News and BleepingComputer reported. The 16-year-old flaw sits in the shadow-MMU code; patch when fixes are available.

stories.headline: CERT/CC warns of hidden admin backdoor in Tenda router firmware
stories.summary: Several firmware versions from Chinese network-device maker Tenda embed an undocumented authentication backdoor (CVE-2026-11405) that grants administrative access to the devices' web management interfaces, the CERT Coordination Center warned via The Hacker News.

stories.headline: Iran-linked hackers deploy new 'Cavern' C2 against Israeli organisations
stories.summary: An Iranian group affiliated with the Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS) is using a previously undocumented modular command-and-control framework dubbed 'Cavern' (aka Cav3rn) to target Israeli organisations, The Hacker News reported.

stories.headline: Fake IT-support calls on Microsoft Teams push EtherRAT malware
stories.summary: Attackers are impersonating IT support in Microsoft Teams calls to trick employees into running commands that install EtherRAT malware, BleepingComputer reported — a reminder to verify support contacts out of band.

stories.headline: Max-severity Adobe ColdFusion flaw now exploited in attacks
stories.summary: A maximum-severity Adobe ColdFusion flaw, CVE-2026-48282 (CVSS 10.0), is being exploited in the wild within hours of disclosure, BleepingComputer reported; Adobe patched it on 1 July and Canada's cyber centre confirmed ongoing attacks. Affected versions include ColdFusion 2025.9, 2023.20 and earlier — patch immediately.

stories.headline: Opera GX flaw let malicious sites silently install data-stealing mods
stories.summary: A flaw in Opera GX, the gaming-focused Opera browser, let a malicious website silently install a browser add-on and lift data from pages a victim visits — in a proof of concept, researchers reconstructed a signed-in user's full Gmail address from a single visit, The Hacker News reported.

stories.headline: 'SkillCloak' lets malicious AI-agent skills evade static scanners
stories.summary: Researchers at HKUST showed that scanners meant to catch malicious add-on 'skills' for AI coding agents can be fooled by simple self-extracting packing changes that leave the malware working — a warning for teams relying on static checks of agent skills, The Hacker News reported.

stories.headline: China-nexus hackers use fake Indian tax-filing utility to deploy DcRAT
stories.summary: A suspected China-nexus cluster is targeting Indian taxpayers, tax professionals and corporate finance teams with a fake tax-filing utility that delivers the DcRAT remote-access trojan to steal data, The Hacker News reported.

stories.headline: 'JadePuffer' ransomware used an AI agent to automate the whole attack
stories.summary: BleepingComputer reported on JadePuffer ransomware that used an AI agent to automate an entire intrusion end to end — an early example of agent-driven attack tooling defenders should watch.
